issues.description: Storing a live FrameProcessor on a control frame couples the frame to mutable runtime identity and risks lifecycle leaks
issues.detail: ServiceSwitcherRequestMetadataFrame.service holds a reference to a FrameProcessor instance. Control frames are typically value-like; embedding a processor reference invites pickling/serialization breakage, garbage-collection retention of swapped-out services, and equality surprises if active_service is later replaced by a wrapper. A service name or id would preserve the invariant ("target the active service") without the coupling.

issues.description: Identity comparison via == on FrameProcessor relies on default object identity and is not stated as an invariant
issues.detail: The suppression rule `frame.service == self.strategy.active_service` works only because FrameProcessor inherits default __eq__. If a subclass ever overrides equality, the switcher silently stops suppressing the frame and downstream sees an internal control frame. State the invariant explicitly (use `is`) or compare by a stable id, and document it.

issues.description: Loop invariant of push_frame's suppression logic is implicit; a one-line literate comment would make it auditable
issues.detail: The new branch needs the reader to reconstruct: "the request frame is emitted only by the targeted service after handling, therefore arriving here means handled-by-active." That chain belongs in the comment. Without it, a future reader cannot tell whether non-active services could also route through here.

issues.description: Forward-reference type "FrameProcessor" on the dataclass field is unresolved and unimported in frames.py
issues.detail: The annotation is a string, so dataclass construction works, but tooling (dataclasses.fields with get_type_hints, pydantic adapters, IDEs) will fail to resolve it unless FrameProcessor is importable in this module's namespace. Either add a TYPE_CHECKING import or weaken the annotation to Any with a docstring contract.

issues.description: Behavior change: non-targeted services now see a ServiceSwitcherRequestMetadataFrame they previously never saw, but only the active service handles it
issues.detail: queue_frame on the active service propagates downstream; STTService now re-pushes the frame after handling. Inactive STT services downstream of the switcher will never receive it (suppressed at push_frame), which is correct — but the contract "only the targeted service acts" should be asserted in STTService's handler too, otherwise a future refactor that broadcasts the frame will cause duplicate metadata emission.

review.summary: The rename and targeting refinement is structurally sound and the test coverage tracks the behavior change. The principal rigor concern is data-structure choice: embedding a live FrameProcessor reference inside a control frame couples a value-like message to mutable runtime identity, and the suppression check leans on default object equality without stating that invariant. A short literate comment on the suppression rule, a stable identifier instead of the processor reference, and a defensive guard in STTService's handler would close the audit. UNDER-AUDITED on invariants; otherwise sound.
